claim: An inbound vendor email's attachment row (conversation_attachments.order_id) carries only the order its Gmail thread names, never the order the handleInboundEmail 2b fallback picked. On origin/main at a323cc80b, rabbitmq-bridge.service.ts passed the fallback's orderId (the provider's newest procurement_orders row whose status is not terminal, read when the gmail_thread_id lookup found no order) to persistAttachments, which wrote it to conversation_attachments.order_id; DocumentIntakeService.sweepUningestedAttachments hands that column to ingest, and linkAndMatch files a document that arrives with an order as a procurement_document_links row with link_method 'manual', confidence 1, so an invoice sent in a fresh thread was filed against whichever order of that vendor was open. Now handleInboundEmail keeps threadOrderId, written only from the thread lookup's outbound[0].order_id, and persistAttachments receives it; the fallback still sets orderId for the conversation row, the notice and the responder. With no order on the attachment, intake runs autoLink, which links only on an exact order_number inside the house ('po_number', 0.95). Static: the verify strips comments, requires exactly one persistAttachments call in handleInboundEmail with (inserted.id, threadOrderId), exactly one write to threadOrderId (outbound[0].order_id), the declaration, the fallback's 'orderId = openOrders[0].id;', and three case names in a-guessed-order-does-not-link-the-paper.spec.ts. Measured 2026-10-07: exit 1 on origin/main a323cc80b's bridge, and exit 1 on each of five static mutants (persistAttachments given orderId; the fallback also writing threadOrderId; the threadOrderId argument line-commented beside an orderId argument; the fallback removed; a spec case renamed); a missing spec file is a Traceback naming No such file or directory (cannot-run). Spec: 7/7 on the branch, 2 of 7 red with main's bridge.
